failures.criterion: Every sentence of the pull request body is true of the code: Change bullet 3 and Look-at-first now say a session name moves 'in exactly two ways' — the 90-day retention running out, or 'an operator re-points the entry that fixes it'. The architect asked whether a third way can be produced.
failures.evidence: A third way exists, and it leaves the configured entry locked out. Each broker replica reserves the names its own configuration fixes once, at its first exchange (Provider.reserveSessions), and ReserveSessions takes a name from whoever holds it; the deployment runs two broker replicas (its broker/deployment.go: Replicas 2). So during a rollout that re-points a fixed name, an old-configuration replica whose first exchange comes after a new replica's — one restarted or evicted mid-rollout, or any old replica that had not exchanged yet — takes the name back, and the new replicas never reserve again. Driven on the real binary, two processes on one database (throwaway probe, $TMPDIR/infra228/probes/r4/zz_tester_r4b_test.go): old config fixes legion-daemon:ACME for example-daemon; new config fixes it for example-other. Old replica: example-daemon exchanges -> 200. New replica starts: example-other exchanges -> 200 (taken). An old-config replica restarts and serves an unrelated exchange (example-worker, b-own) -> 200, logging `WARN broker: the token exchange took a session name the configuration fixes from its holder session=legion-daemon:ACME from=account:…:example-other to=account:…:example-daemon`. After the rollout, on the new replica: example-other, the entry the configuration now fixes the name for, -> 400 invalid_grant; example-daemon, no longer fixed, asking the name -> 200. The name is held 'infinity' for the old principal and stays so until a new-configuration replica restarts. No operator re-pointed anything at that moment, so the body's 'exactly two ways' is false, and the outcome is the class the reviewer's finding 1 was about (a fixed entry's own caller refused). How to close it is the architect's call: the body names this path, or the code makes a replica's own configured principal win its fixed name when it is refused it (for example, re-reserving that name inside the claim when the asking principal is the one this replica's configuration fixes it for). No red test is committed for the behaviour, because the architect has ruled that a new finding after this round may go to a child issue, and a red test here would turn this branch's required test job red regardless of that decision; the probe above is the reproduction.
